content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (2024-06-24):
- History: Prices have been declining from ~74.6 to ~68 over 18 days
- Sentiment: Mix of positive/negative, ending with 0.67
- Model forecasts: Start at 67.82, gradually increasing to ~72 by day 7, then stable around 70-71
- True outcomes: Start at 67.56, declining more sharply to ~64.8 by day 20

The model is too high! It's not declining fast enough. The true prices are falling faster than the model predicts.

Example 2 (2024-06-25):
- Very similar to Example 1, just 1 day later
- Model forecasts: [67.77, 67.20, 66.63, 67.51, 68.63, 71.37, 71.50, 71.06, 71.40, 70.23, 69.86, 69.32, 69.67, 70.31, 68.40, 68.27, 66.54, 66.09, 66.10, 65.16, 66.28, 69.60, 68.26, 69.24, 70.70, 71.09, 72.47, 75.10, 75.23, 74.49]
- True outcomes: [67.80, 67.23, 66.49, 67.36, 68.33, 70.93, 70.91, 70.18, 70.35, 69.04, 68.52, 67.96, 68.52, 69.35, 67.58, 67.94, 66.42, 66.11, 66.00, 64.79, 65.79, 68.90, 67.08, 67.71, 68.78, 68.58, 69.24, 71.17, 70.44, 68.86]


- The errors are nearly identical to Example 1, confirming a consistent pattern
